question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund implements convertible arb: invests INR 1 cr in 12% convertible bonds (20% equity capital of INR 20 lakh + 80% borrowed at 10% p.a.). Shorts 50,000 equity shares at INR 40 (borrow fee INR 5/share). Over 1 year: coupon INR 12 lakh, borrow cost INR 8 lakh, borrow fee INR 2.5 lakh, dividend forgone INR 1 lakh, conversion/equity P&L net INR 5 lakh. What is the ROI on the INR 20 lakh fund capital?

explanation.text: The Logic: Net income = +12 - 8 - 2.5 - 1 + 5 = +5.5 lakh. ROI = 5.5 / 20 = 27.50% (PDF Example 10.6 matches). Note ROI is on the 20 lakh equity capital, not on the 1 cr gross position — that's the leverage multiplier. The Trap: Option A is coupon yield. Option B omits one expense. Option D double-counts. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C uses the same example. VIII (Derivatives) tests the embedded-call delta.
